The Best Gaming Mouse

Wired November 26, 2026

All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.

Picking a gaming mouse can be difficult. There are countless metrics to factor in and a nearly unlimited number of mice with unique approaches in defining what's best. Quite honestly, it’s a market rife with opportunities for analysis paralysis to take hold.

That’s why I take the time to test countless gaming mice—to tell you what works and what doesn’t. I can’t say precisely which mouse will work for you—that’s dependent not only on technical specs but on your preferences, needs, budget, and hand size—but hopefully I can provide some insights into the top options out there, what's the best for specific types of gamers, and why I’ve picked them.

Be sure to read our other peripheral buying guides for more, including the Best Ergonomic Mouse, Best Gaming Headsets, Best Mechanical Keyboards, and Best Hall Effect Keyboards.

Updated November 2026: I've added the Razer Basilisk V4 Pro and Wallhack M-001. I've also included the Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike in my honorable mentions, reorganized the list, and updated prices.

Razer

Amazon

Razer

Best Buy

The Razer Cobra HyperSpeed (9/10, WIRED Recommends) is far more reasonable and practical than most of the ultra-light options today. Instead of shaving down features and mass to make the simplest mouse possible, the Cobra Hyperspeed finds an ideal middle ground, maintaining features like RGB lighting, Bluetooth connectivity, and options for wireless charging. Despite that, it still weighs below 70 grams, a number that was unbelievable for even the most premium wireless mice a decade ago. Inside, it’s packing an optical sensor, optical switches, and an optical scroll wheel—all top-of-the-line parts that are some of the fastest and most reliable on the market. While the mouse is limited to 1,000-Hz polling with the included low-profile USB-A dongle (which I prefer for convenience), it can be upgraded to 8,000 Hz with the bulkier and less-convenient HyperPolling dongle, cutting out its only serious limitation.

Beyond that, this mouse can do practically everything. It works as a travel mouse, a permanent desktop solution, and is even compatible with Razer’s wireless charging pucks, which lets you charge the mouse using either the Mouse Dock Pro, which ups your polling rate to 8,000 Hz, or the HyperFlux V2 wireless charging mousepad. The simple, symmetrical shape is comfortable and easy to hold, with the curved buttons on top creating spots to rest your fingers, while the low, gradual curve feels natural for resting your palm. Plus, its near-symmetry means it can be used as an ambidextrous mouse in a pinch (although lefties will miss out on the side buttons).

Wallhack

Wallhack

While the price may be steep, Wallhack’s M-001 (9/10, WIRED Recommends) is one of the best I’ve tested in a long time. Although the specs aren’t quite cutting-edge (the sensor is a bit outdated, and some of the internals are still mechanical instead of optical), every aspect of this mouse’s user experience has been fine-tuned to perfection. That's what sets it apart for me.

The mouse itself is made entirely from magnesium, and the outer shell doesn’t feature any of the large weight-saving cutouts used by similar mice from Corsair, AngryMiao, and even Razer. Instead, the upper is entirely solid, and all of the cutouts are on the underside of the mouse. Because of this, the battery can be swapped out within seconds.

Alongside the mouse itself, the M-001’s dongle is one of the best on the market. Instead of simply sitting on a desk, this dongle incorporates physical dials to adjust the mouse’s sensitivity and polling rate, and recharges the spare battery when not in use.

While it may be silly, my favorite feature of this mouse is the swappable batteries themselves. Similar to a Nintendo Switch cartridge or an SD card, the batteries feature a push-lock mechanism that’s robust, satisfying, and intuitive, improving significantly on the magnet or rotation-lock systems that other swappable mouse batteries use.

SteelSeries

Amazon (Wired)

Amazon (Wireless)

The Rival 3 (7/10, WIRED Recommends) is a simple, no-frills gaming mouse. It’s lightweight, robust, and pretty much hits all the marks for gaming: Easy-access side buttons, clicky main buttons, underside RGB lighting, and a grippy rubberized scroll wheel. This SteelSeries mouse doesn’t innovate much, but like a Toyota Camry, it’s simple and reliable enough to get nearly anything done. At a price below $50, you’re getting all the performance you can realistically use for non-professional gaming. There aren’t any unnecessary features that add complication, and the mouse can be fully disassembled in under five minutes with a set of Phillips and Torx screwdrivers.

Razer

Amazon

Best Buy

Razer

The Razer Viper V4 Pro (9/10, WIRED Recommends) is the latest installment in a long line of fantastic competitive mice, offering performance improvements across every metric. Along with top-of-the-line specs, optical sensors across the board, and a great symmetrical shape, the V4 also incorporates the same spherical dongle included with the Deathadder V4 Pro, which maintains its 8,000-Hz polling while adding LED indicators for information like connection quality, battery life, and DPI stage.

Using the exact same shape as the V3, this mouse is comfortable and intuitive to use. The shape is easy to move around, with small curves on the mouse buttons for your fingertips to rest, and the curvature of the sides creates natural spots for your thumb and pinky. The Razer Synapse software is one of the most powerful and intuitive on the market. There are customization options for mouse dpi, tracking distance, dynamic sensitivity, and even adjusting the mouse sensor to accommodate a rotated grip.

The only downside of the Viper V4 Pro is how uncompromising it is— there's no Bluetooth, and the included 2.4-GHz dongle requires a USB-A to USB-C cable (included) that runs to your computer, with no option for a smaller USB-A dongle (last seen on the V2). These decisions were made to lighten the mouse and improve connection quality, but they can be inconvenient if you need a wireless gaming mouse to pair with a laptop.

AngryMiao

Amazon

AngryMiao

The Infinity .97 is one of the lightest mice I’ve tested at only 48.3 grams (without the removable rear panel, which adds 3.8 grams), and one of the sturdiest thanks to its magnesium upper shell. While the skeletal shape may look off-putting at first, it was far more comfortable and usable than I would have expected, especially when used with a fingertip grip. However, anyone dedicated to a palm or claw grip will likely be better served by a larger mouse with a sturdier back end.

Beyond weight, this mouse has fantastic specs: 8,000-Hz polling, optical switches, and a rating of 0.2 ms of latency all put it on par with Razer and Logitech’s best offerings. The most impressive feature by far is the removable and magnetically hot-swappable batteries that recharge using the mouse’s 2.4G dongle. This eliminates downtime from a dead battery and reduces the risks of long-term battery degradation and failure (assuming AngryMiao continues to sell spares).

While the styling is certainly more of an acquired taste, the large gaps result in a shape that’s rigid and better-looking than the usual uniform, hexagon-shaped holes. The shape is shockingly comfortable despite the gaps (which are placed to preserve typical touch points), and the removable rear “hatchback” panel finds a reasonable balance between a standard shape and the ultra-lightweight “fingertip mice” that have become more popular in recent years.

The software is also shockingly robust, with expected adjustments for DPI, polling, macros, and so on, alongside more granular adjustments like debounce speed, motion sync, ripple correction, and a Blast Mode that sets the mouse’s internal sensor to its maximum speed of 20,000 Hz. (It’s worth noting that the mouse still communicates with your computer at 8,000 Hz—this simply provides more data from the sensor to the mouse). Also, unlike some similarly-priced offerings, this mouse has both 2.4G and Bluetooth connectivity.

Razer

Amazon

The Basilisk V3 Pro was a fantastic mouse, and the V4 Pro significantly improves the technical specs while maintaining some of the best features. Primarily, the V4 Pro has an absurdly-high 8,000-Hz polling rate and a scroll wheel with smooth, ratcheted, and “high-sensitivity” scrolling options. This mouse also maintains the same four-button layout on the side, and has a larger shape with an integrated thumb rest for comfortable long-term use.

As far as comfort and practicality, the Basilisk’s sculpted shape and thumb rest feel more like an office mouse than a gaming mouse, but the curved mouse buttons and smooth overall shape mean a claw grip still isn’t out of the question. The mouse wheel also has horizontal scrolling that’s activated by tilting it to the left or right, and the large number of programmable side buttons are great for both gaming and multimedia editing. While it’s still fairly hefty at 98 grams, this mouse is great if you’re either ambivalent about weight and want something more ergonomic, or if you prefer a heavier mouse. It might not be worth an upgrade when coming from the previous model, though, given the price.

Logitech

Amazon

Logitech

Best Buy

The Pro X Superlight 2C is only marginally smaller than the standard Superlight 2, and weighs 51 grams, a 15 percent drop. It's essentially a scaled-down version. They are both capable of 8,000-Hz polling, use the same 44,000 dots-per-inch Hero 2 sensor, and have the same quoted 95-hour battery life. Because the 2C packs all this into a smaller package, it’s ideal for people with smaller hands, or anyone who primarily plays using a claw grip and doesn’t need the extra weight.

It's not a travel-size mouse, but I think the 2C is better suited than most ultralight mice on this list. It uses a small USB-A dongle that can slot into a removable panel on the underside of the mouse for transport, and the shell is fairly sturdy. I wouldn’t toss it into a checked bag at the airport or wedge it into a side pocket, but it should hold up for light travel.

Razer

Amazon

Razer

Best Buy

A larger, sculpted alternative to the Viper V4 Pro, the DeathAdder V4 Pro (9/10, WIRED Recommends) is a fantastic mouse that’s a tiny bit heavier, but potentially more comfortable than its smaller cousin. If you prefer the shape and feel of a sculpted mouse, this is a great alternative to Razer’s flagship competitive model that packs comparable performance and is equally-loaded with premium optical internals. The two share the same in-depth customization options, with adjustments for sensitivity curves, lift-off and landing distance, and the ability to adjust the mouse’s rotation for different grip styles.

The Deathadder V4 Pro also introduced Razer’s spherical USB-C dongle with three RGB lights that can be adjusted to display information like polling rate, battery level, connection quality, or DPI. While the colored light system can be a bit abstract, it provides functionality to an accessory that’s going to be on your desk no matter what, and makes it easier to keep track of the settings on this ultra-lightweight mouse. Plus, I find it looks a lot more natural than most dongles available today. Much like other competitive-focused options on this list, the only real issue with this mouse is the lack of Bluetooth connectivity, a weight-savings measure that makes sense for competitive use, but can be a bit annoying for certain users and setups that demand more flexibility.

Logitech G Pro X3 Superstrike for $200: This is a major advancement in mouse tech, so much so that I’d consider it one of the most significant gaming mouse developments in recent years. This technology replaces the typical mechanical or optical switches under a mouse’s main buttons with analog switches, similar to those on a Hall effect keyboard, that allow for the actuation distance of the button to be customized. Because these linear switches no longer have a “click” sensation, the Superstrike pairs them with artificial haptic feedback. This activates when the button registers an input, and the intensity of the feedback can be customized across X levels.

However, I don’t personally like this mouse. The haptic feedback feels uncanny, since it shakes the entire mouse instead of creating a real “click” sensation, and the added complexity isn’t worth the relatively minor fine-tuning capabilities. However, I can recognize the benefits of the technology, and I can absolutely understand why some people might love this mouse.

Steelseries Rival Pro Wireless for $180: While the specs aren’t groundbreaking compared to other light mice, and the “ultra-polling” technology doesn’t offer a proven benefit over competitors, the Rival Wireless maintains the fantastic shape of previous installments in the Rival 300 line. If you’ve found other sculpted ultralight offerings from Razer and Logitech to be a bit lacking, this could be the option for you.

Razer Basilisk V3 Pro for $120: Razer’s previous installment in the Basilisk line is still a really solid option. This mouse is comfortable, convenient, loaded with features, and it looks sleek on any desk. It’s also featured in our Best Ergonomic Mouse guide, but it performs so well that I had to include it here. Razer’s optical sensor is capable of up to 35,000 dpi, and the mouse has polling up to 1,000 Hz (or up to 8,000 Hz with a HyperPolling dongle). As far as comfort and practicality, the Basilisk’s sculpted shape and thumb rest feel more like an office mouse than a gaming mouse, but the curved mouse buttons and smooth overall shape mean a claw grip still isn’t out of the question.

Corsair Sabre V2 Pro Ultralight for $200: When I first reviewed the new 36-gram Sabre, I was wowed by its weight but critical of its overly thin shell and flimsy construction. However, I accepted these as being a part of its innate nature as the lightest-possible mouse, and I’m incredibly glad that it exists. It’s a great option if you’re willing to sacrifice everything in the name of “simplifying and adding lightness,” as car designer Colin Chapman put it. But it's probably not the right choice if you want something that feels substantial or meaningful beyond that.

Corsair Sabre V2 Carbon Fiber and Magnesium for $170: While neither of these carry the same groundbreaking lightness of their predecessor (they both hover just below the 60-gram mark), they offer a much more refined design with premium materials and rigidity that’s unmatched by Corsair’s mainstream competitors. While they lag a bit behind in performance, they both feel fantastic to fling around a desk while providing a much more sturdy chassis that gives the impression they can withstand some serious use. Unless you really love the looks or science of carbon fiber, the less-expensive magnesium chassis is definitely the way to go in terms of both sturdiness and on-desk appeal.

Logitech Pro X Superlight 2 Dex for $150: This sculpted mouse predates the Deathadder V4 Pro by over a year and, because of this, the specs lag slightly behind it. However, the shape is just as comfortable, and the internals are still fantastic for anyone except the absolute most-discerning. The best part of this mouse is that, these days, it can easily be found on a significant discount. If you don’t want to shell out the extra cash for Razer’s latest model, or if you prefer Logitech’s software and styling, this is the mouse for you.

Corsair Scimitar Elite Wireless SE for $70: While MMO-focused mice aren’t finding themselves in the spotlight anymore (much like many of the MMOs that required numpads, and even numpads themselves, for that matter), there are still a few new models kicking around. The Scimitar is one of the most modern ones, adding adjustability to the classic numpad-on-the-side formula with a sliding rail to accommodate different grip styles and hand sizes. While this mouse obviously doesn’t compete with other models on this list in terms of technical specs or weight, it’s a really great mouse for the kinds of games that still necessitate having swathes of macros at your fingertips.

Steelseries Aerox 3 for $100: While it doesn’t have nearly the same weight or speed advantages as offerings from Razer and Logitech, the Aerox 3 is still a great mouse in its own special way. Weighing in at only 66 grams and being one of the only waterproof mice on this list (I literally ran it under a sink for a couple minutes to test this), this mouse is great for multi-user gaming computers, accident-prone individuals, and/or the poolside gaming setup of your dreams. Plus, built-in Bluetooth connectivity means you aren’t stuck with a dongle! However, 1000 Hz polling and 18,000 DPI do mean that, if you aren’t looking for something that’s more durable than average, you may be able to get a good bit more performance for a comparable price.

Logitech G203 for $20: Budget gaming mice often forgo a lot of the conveniences and performance you get out of nicer models, but the Logitech G203 never feels like it's lacking. The sensor has a lower maximum sensitivity than you'll get out of a more expensive offering—8,000 dots per inch—so if you need that top-end sensitivity, you'll want to look elsewhere, but it features six buttons, compatibility with Logitech’s G Hub software, and, most importantly, has RGB lighting. Those are all things you'd typically expect to pay more for.

Razer Viper V3 Pro for $100: The previous-gen Viper V3 Pro remains a good choice for competitive gamers, especially since it's selling for much less than the newer model. It remains an uncompromising mouse for lightweight, high-speed gaming performance. Despite being a couple of years old at this point, it still has competitive specs, the same great symmetrical shape, and some of the best-feeling buttons on the market. The battery lasts an incredibly long time (it’s rated for over 95 hours, and I didn’t need to charge it once during my testing). And with the included HyperPolling dongle, the mouse is capable of up to 8,000-Hz polling.

One of the cheapest things you can do to upgrade your PC gaming experience is to invest in a high-quality mousepad. If you’re a mouse-and-keyboard gamer, having the right surface for your trusty little rodent can be super helpful. Not only do you have a nice little area of your desk cordoned off for mouse use, but you also get a surface designed to be as friction-free and slick as possible—so you’ll be as quick as possible.

Harber London Professional Leather Desk Mat

Harber London Professional Leather Desk Mat for $239: Despite more than a year of use, this Harber London leather desk mat still looks exquisite. The pebbled leather is supple and has a nice texture, but your mouse will glide over it effortlessly. It comes in three sizes and three colors.

SteelSeries QcK Mouse Pad for $11: SteelSeries’ QcK mousepad is one of my all-time favorites. The medium size is perfect for most desks, even small ones. It’s well-made and doesn’t fray easily—cheaper mousepads often fray at the edges, which ruins the aesthetic a good mousepad can lend to a workstation.

Grovemade Wool Felt Desk Pad for $70: This doesn't seem like your usual gaming accessory, because it's not. It's a wool felt pad from Portland, Oregon, company Grovemade, and it's large enough to fit a keyboard and a mouse with room to spare. It feels soft and plush under your wrists, and all of the gaming mice on this list just glide over its surface; it's like they're sliding on glass. It's a big surprise, honestly. Not to mention, a felt desk pad adds an air of sophistication and style to any desk, without making it seem too uptight. The color looks amazing under RGB lighting in a dark room. It's an easy and affordable way to inject some unique style into your work (and play) space.

What Makes a Good Gaming Mouse?

Here are a few features that really separate a gaming mouse from a regular came-with-my-PC kind of mouse:

Extra-sensitive optical sensors: Gaming mice should have more sensitive optical sensors that can detect smaller movements more quickly than a standard mouse.

More buttons: At a minimum, a good gaming mouse should have a clickable scroll wheel, a button for adjusting sensitivity, and two buttons where your thumb rests. Those extra thumb buttons can be lifesavers in competitive games.

Better buttons: They should also have higher-quality buttons, and more of them, than a standard office mouse. The left and right buttons should have individual switches inside, tensioned to register rapid clicks and reinforced to withstand more frequent clicks than a normal mouse. Top-of-the-line gaming mice often feature proprietary mechanical switches inside that give them a more tactile feel when you click.

Polling rate: For most games, the typical 1,000-Hz polling rate will be sufficient, but if you play a lot of fast-paced competitive games, where split-second actions can be crucial to victory, than you may get some benefit out of mice with faster polling rates.

Don't buy the DPI hype: Dots per inch (DPI) is a metric that describes a mouse’s overall sensitivity. A higher dpi means it can respond quicker, which is helpful in competitive online games. However, even if your mouse can go all the way up to, say, 20,000 dpi, most people (even in online games) keep their sensitivity around 1,000 to 1,600 dpi. More doesn’t necessarily mean better.

Your Palm Size and Grip Style Matters

A major aspect when shopping for a gaming mouse is size. Using a mouse that’s too small for your hand can cause strain on your hand and wrist, while a mouse that’s too large can feel unwieldy and be difficult to move precisely. It’s important to measure your hand and take into account the grip style you plan to use.

There are three primary mouse grips: Palm grip, claw grip, and fingertip grip. Palm grip is typically considered the most accurate but least agile, and it’s how most people use their mouse day-to-day. Your entire hand sits on the mouse, with your palm resting on the back half and your fingers laid along the mouse buttons. Claw grip is more agile, but will sacrifice some accuracy and stability. For this grip, you rest the bottom of your hand against the mouse while bending your fingers into a claw-like shape, leaving a significant amount of open air between your fingertips and the back of your hand. Fingertip grip has the least contact and allows for the most agility, but also sacrifices even more stability. With this grip, your hand will hover over the mouse, with your fingertips resting on the mouse buttons, and your thumb and pinky finger gripping the mouse from either side.

For a standard mouse used with a palm grip, the best way to determine the correct size is to measure the distance from the tip of your middle finger to the bottom of your palm, and compare those numbers to an online guide. Rocket Jump Ninja has a helpful tool for this, which also provides measurements of the recommended mice for cross-referencing. Alternatively, I’ve found it helpful to hold your hand in an arc as if you’re holding a mouse, and measure the distance from the bottom of your palm to your fingertips to get a measurement you can directly compare to mouse length. This method can also work for claw grip, but since the bottom of your palm will be resting directly on the mouse instead of sitting at the back, I find it better to err on the side of caution and pick a mouse that’s a few millimeters longer than you need.

Mouse sizing is dependent on the type of mouse you’re looking for: Whether chasing lightness or portability, there are quite a few short and small mice on the market. Compact or fingertip-grip mice like the Razer Basilisk Mobile or the G-Wolves Fenrir won’t fit the standard recommendations of mouse measurements. Instead, for a mouse like this (or any mouse you plan to use with a fingertip grip), I find it best to compare the mouse’s width to the distance between your thumb and your pinky finger (or your ring finger, depending on how you hold a mouse) in a comfortable gripping position. A mouse that’s too narrow can cause strain on your hand, while one that’s too wide can be difficult to properly grip and move.

The Best Black Friday Deals on Amazon Devices

My house has been powered by Alexa and Amazon devices to some degree for the past decade. There's always an Alexa somewhere in my house, ready for a quick command, and it's an ecosystem I find myself coming back to again and again—especially since Amazon always has something new coming out to catch my eye.

While not everything is on sale from Amazon's various ecosystems (sorry if you've got an eye on one of the newest Kindles; those have yet to be on sale), there are several great Amazon devices you can get for a better price than ever during Black Friday. Here are all the best deals I've found on Amazon devices.

Looking for more discounts? Don't miss our guide to the Absolute Best Black Friday Deals. Hunting for Kindles and e-reader deals specifically? I've got a story for that, too.

Amazon

Amazon

This is my new bedside companion. The Echo Time feels more like a second-generation Echo Spot than the actual Echo Spot that came out two years ago; I'm curious why they didn't just make this a third-gen Spot. The Echo Time brings back the larger screen of the original Echo Spot and has a fun range of customizable clock faces you can use. It has sleep sensing to wake you up in the half-hour window before your official alarm time. You'll have to place it perfectly for that feature to work, but I've liked it a lot more than I expected. It also has no camera, so you can put it in your bedroom without any worries. It's expensive for what it is, so now is a great time to pick one up for yourself.

Black Friday is here, and we're seeing some great deals on our favorite tech, including AirPods. Both the flagship AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2 are on sale, knocking up to $130 off their regular prices. Whether you want pocketable earbuds for everyday use, premium noise-canceling headphones, or seamless Apple integration, these are some of the best prices I've seen recently. I don't expect these prices to go back up until after Cyber Monday, but with tech getting more expensive, I wouldn't wait too long if you've been planning to upgrade.

Want more deals? Check out our guide to the Best Black Friday Headphone Deals, the Best Black Friday Deals Under $100, and the Absolute Best Black Friday Deals.

Apple

Amazon

Walmart

Apple

The flagship AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s best AirPods yet. Upgrades include stronger noise-canceling, a new acoustic architecture for deeper bass, and redesigned ear tips for a more secure fit. The ear tips also keep my AirPods from slipping during longer runs and sweatier workouts. New tools include a built-in heart rate sensor for fitness tracking, live translation, and a camera remote to snap photos or videos on your iPhone. These earbuds are also the first AirPods to be IP57 rated against dust, sweat, and rain.

At the time of writing, they are 40 percent off at Amazon, Best Buy, Target, and Walmart. This is the lowest price I’ve ever seen them drop to. In other words, I’d grab a pair now if they’re on your wish list.

Apple

Amazon

Walmart

Apple

The AirPods Max 2’s newer H2 chip improves active noise cancellation and transparency mode and enables a suite of intelligent features, including conversation awareness, live translation, and improved Siri interactions. The AirPods Max 2 are designed with a new high-dynamic-range amplifier for deeper bass, more natural vocals, and cleaner highs. The ear cuffs, while plush and comfortable for longer listening sessions, do trap some heat, but I have yet to find a pair of over-ear headphones that don’t.

At $549, the AirPods Max 2 can be a tough sell, especially with so many excellent, more affordable alternatives on the market. But at $130 off, they’re a lot easier to justify, especially if you want the seamless integration that comes with Apple’s ecosystem.

Wired November 27, 2026

All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.

Everyone I know is scaling back for Christmas this year. Personally, I'm focusing on buying practical items and secondhand goods. And I know I'm not alone in the struggle, so I'm extra cognizant of my local toy and supply drives too. Black Friday is a great time to buy flashy tech and fun extravagances, but household necessities are on sale as well.

I've rounded up deals on the Reviews team’s must-haves, plus highlighted some very affordable toys that you might want to pick up to donate. If your favorite brand isn't listed, it's still worth looking up to see if there's a notable discount. ’Tis the season! For more discounts, check out our roundup of the Absolute Best Black Friday Deals.

Noco

Amazon

Walmart

This itty-bitty jump starter can fit in any trunk, if not the glove box, and it packs enough power to jump a vehicle up to six times. It's an essential if you live somewhere that experiences inclement weather, but it's also just smart to keep one of these around for general emergency and disaster preparedness.

Dawn

Amazon

It's rare that we all agree, but the WIRED Reviews team is full of Dawn Powerwash enthusiasts. You spray what you need and don't have to deal with messy drips and slippery bottles. It's also a great degreaser for your car, your patio furniture, or your yucky bathtub. And it comes with refills.

Play-Doh

Amazon

Toy drives can be tricky because popular toys are so darn expensive, but I've never met a kid who didn't like Play-Doh. (Spoken as a 33-year-old kid myself.) This pack comes with 12 cans of bright and fun colors that would certainly make a great addition to any donation box. You could also split it up for stocking stuffers.

The Best Black Friday Mattress Deals

Wired November 27, 2026

All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.

Mattress sales come and go so often that it’s hard to determine what’s an actual deal. The times of year when we see the most legit mattress deals are Black Friday, Cyber Monday, Memorial Day, and Labor Day. And this year is no different. We’re seeing our favorite WIRED-tested bedding and mattress brands offering some of the best Black Friday deals and discounts we've seen this year. I’ll be gathering more mattress deals throughout the weekend, so be sure to check back often for fresh discounts on these often-pricey purchases.

Note that all mattress prices below are for queen sizes unless otherwise noted, and discounts on Shop may only appear once you're in the checkout menu.

Want more deals? Check out our guide to the Best Early Black Friday Deals on Amazon, the Best Early Black Friday TV Deals, and Black Friday Deals at Home Depot.

Updated November 27, 2026: I've updated mattress sales with new dates and promo codes, updated prices, and added new deals from Molecule, Organica, Layla, Perfectly Snug, Amerisleep, and Buffy.

Helix Sleep

Helix Sleep

This Helix mattress has been our top pick for years and remains one of the most popular bed-in-a-box options for good reason. Its plush pillow top and medium-firm feel make it comfortable for nearly any sleeper, whether they sleep on their side, back, or stomach.

We love Helix in general, and right now the brand has 20 percent off site-wide when you use the Helix promo code BF20. It also offers special discounts, including 25 percent off Luxe mattresses with promo code LUXE25 and 30 percent off Elite mattresses with code ELITE30. (All listed Helix promo codes are valid through November 29.)

Birch

Birch

We really love this organic mattress. When we tested the Luxe model above, we found it offered a lovely balance of plush comfort and pressure relief, with just enough bounce to make it a great choice for back sleepers seeking a little extra support. But all of Birch's models are made from natural materials like wool, latex, and cotton, without any polyurethane-based foams.

Birch's Black Friday sale runs through November 29, with 25 percent off site-wide when you use the Birch promo code BF25.

Bear

Bear

The firm Bear Elite Hybrid has long been one of our top picks for back pain. Both reviewers who tested it agree that you love it more the longer you sleep on it. Bear mattresses also keep you cool, with phase-change material that absorbs body heat and copper-infused memory foam that wicks it away.

Bear Mattress has a Black Friday Sale running through November 29, with 35 percent off site-wide and a free bundle of two pillows and a mattress protector with promo code BF35.

Nolah

Shop

Nolah

This was former WIRED reviewer (and sleep expert) Julia Forbes’ all-time favorite mattress. She appreciated that its extra springiness provided added support and firmness, making it ideal for side sleepers.

Nolah Mattress’ Black Friday sale runs through November 29, with 35 percent off site-wide; no promo code needed.

Leesa

Shop

Leesa

We on the WIRED Reviews team love hybrid mattresses because they bring together the best of both worlds—memory foam and the support of inner coils. The Sapira Chill is the best hybrid mattress we've tested to date, bringing relief to our tester's back pain while absorbing excess heat through the temperature-regulating cover.

Leesa Sleep’s Black Friday Sale runs through December 8 and offers 30 percent off mattresses and 35 percent off adjustable base bundles, with no promo code needed.

Brooklyn Bedding

Brooklyn Bedding

Hybrids run cooler in general due to the open-spring design, and this cooling hybrid bed has a pillow top to provide a memory-foam-like feel—the best of both worlds. The initial pillow-top layer is made of ThermoPhase “cooling foam,” and the deep dimples on the top create extra airflow to keep things cool. There are 8-inch zoned coils below to give more solid support, and these beds tend to run on the firmer side, so keep that in mind when choosing between soft, medium, or firm.

During Brooklyn Bedding’s Black Friday Sale, you’ll get 30 percent off site-wide through November 29.

Brooklyn Bedding

Brooklyn Bedding

This cooling mattress is infused with copper particles to help wick moisture and provide heat regulation and dispersal.

Brooklyn Bedding

Brooklyn Bedding

This lightweight kids’ mattress is a great option for younger kids transitioning to their own bed or for use in bunk beds and trundles.

Bryte

Bryte

Instead of air chambers on each side of the mattress, as most smart beds use, Bryte uses a more traditional foundation of coils and memory foam layers. They call their coils “Bryte Balancers,” which can be adjusted for things like lumbar support or contouring, down to individual zones, in the connected app. There are also 100 firmness levels, so you can really dial in the settings to optimize for anything, stomach sleepers or folks with back pain included. The bed also tracks your sleep and provides sleep metrics like sleep phases, hours of sleep, heart rate, respiratory rate, and the number of bed rebalances.

The Bryte mattress sale offers 20 percent off site-wide and a free Cozy Earth Bamboo Cooling Sheet Set with purchase, through November 29.

Sleep Number

Sleep Number

Sleep Number

Sleep Number

We love these smart beds from Sleep Number. (Read our review of the ComfortNext Lux Smart Bed here.) They offer balanced pressure that’s ideal for side sleepers, plus cushioning for pressure points, motion isolation, helpful sleep tracking, and customizable firmness. The ComfortNext even has built-in sleep tracking, which monitors your nightly sleep score, called your “SleepIQ” score, within the app. That data is compared with the firmness level you choose, known as your “Sleep Number” setting. This helps you fine-tune the firmness that, based on your sleep-tracking data, helps you sleep better.

The ComfortNext line, including the Lux Smart Bed model above, is 20 percent off. Sleep Number's Climate Collection is 25 percent off, and sheet sets and pillows are BOGO 50 percent off—check out all of Sleep Number's current sales and eligible items here. The offer runs through December 7, and no promo code is needed.

Tempur-Pedic

Tempur-Pedic

Shop

This is probably the most luxurious smart bed the WIRED Reviews team has ever tested. (Read our review here.) You're probably not planning to drop 10 grand on a bed today, but if you've been curious about smart beds, this may be a good one to check out. It has a unique design centered on temperature control, with built-in fans that make its surface noticeably cooler to the touch. The bed also monitors your bedroom's air quality and analyzes sleep metrics with an AI-powered sleep coach to give you feedback.

You can save $500 and get a $300 credit toward a future purchase when you buy a Tempur-ActiveBreeze System, Tempur-Breeze, or Tempur-LuxeAdapt mattress and a Tempur-Ergo Smart Base through December 1, with no promo code necessary.

Bedgear

Shop

Bedgear

When I die, bury me with this modular, supremely cooling mattress. It's part of Bedgear's new Night Ice collection, the coolest beds I've ever slept on. It has a silky cover that's cool to the touch, top layers that work together to dissipate heat effectively, and side mesh vents to increase airflow throughout the mattress. You can choose the same or different levels of firmness on both sides of the mattress.

The M5 above, plus Hybrid Performance and Sport Performance models below, are all discounted, and you can get a further discount if you buy one with an adjustable base. Sales run through December 7.

Bedgear

DreamCloud

Former WIRED reviewer (and sleep expert) Julia Forbes thought this responsive hybrid mattress delivered firm support that helped with spine alignment and good pressure relief. (Read the review here.) The quilted top foam layer contours the hips and chest, and the layers of foam and pocketed coils offer good lumbar support, making it ideal for stomach sleepers or those with back pain.

During DreamCloud's Black Friday Sale, you can get up to 60 percent off mattresses and $100 off all memory foam mattresses.

Plank

During Plank’s Black Friday Sale, you’ll get 30 percent off site-wide through November 29.

Essentia

Essentia

Shop

This luxe model from Essentia was the first organic mattress I tested, and I’ve been spoiled since. The Tatami is vegan, so it contains no wool or other animal byproducts. It also has a nontoxic, allergy-free Kevlar fabric barrier. It doesn't have springs, but it's super comfortable, and its foam gently conforms to your body’s curves and pressure points.

Essentia’s Black Friday sale runs through November 29, with 25 percent off site-wide, and you’ll get two free latex Cloud pillows (a $399 value) with the purchase of a mattress.

Naturepedic

Naturepedic

We recommend this customizable organic mattress for side sleepers as an especially great option for couples. Its modular design lets each person choose a different firmness level, with a top cover that holds separate layers of foam and wrapped coils in place. You can adjust the firmness on either side of the bed to suit your individual preferences. During the 100-night trial, you can swap comfort layers for free to try a different firmness, to ensure you've found the perfect feel.

Naturepedic's Black Friday Sale runs through tonight and offers 20 percent off site-wide, plus 25 percent off all bedding and the Concerto Organic Pillowtop Mattress, with no promo code needed.

Amerisleep

Amerisleep

If you’re looking for an organic mattress that will last a long time, this US-made bed offers a 100-night trial, a 20-year warranty, free shipping, and free returns. It's made with nontoxic, fiberglass-free materials and carries the certifications you want in an organic mattress, including Standard 100 Oeko-Tex, Rainforest Alliance, and Eco-Institut. While this organic mattress was too plush for my taste, if you’re looking for a softer option, it’s a solid and surprisingly affordable choice.

During Amerisleep’s Black Friday Sale, you can get $600 off select mattresses and 40 percent off adjustable bed frames with a mattress purchase with code BFCM, 20 percent off pillows and bamboo sheets with code BFCM20, and 40 percent off upholstered bed frames with a mattress purchase and 25 percent off mattress toppers, with no code needed.

Molecule

Molecule

This copper-infused hybrid mattress aims to move heat away, while coils add lift and stability for better back support. The five zones of RecoveryFLO provide even more support and breathability underneath, and it also features AirTEC foam with enhanced airflow compared to traditional memory foam. It has a medium-firm feel and is also available in all-foam.

Molecule's Black Friday Sale runs through November 27, with $800 off the Engage Elite 14-inch mattress, $300 off the Reflex Elite 14-inch and Engage 12/13-inch mattresses, $200 off CopperWell mattresses, 40 percent off sateen performance sheets, and 30 percent off the CopperWell Topper & Pillow, using code BF26.

Zinus

Amazon

It feels plusher—perhaps medium-soft—than its listed medium firmness, so I'd recommend this bed to people who prefer a plush feel. It has four layers of hypoallergenic, green-tea-infused gel memory foam, along with low motion transfer and a breathable design to help you sleep cool.

Zinus's Amazon deals offer up to 30 percent off select mattresses and bed frames and run until November 30.

The 143 Best Black Friday Deals Have Landed

Wired November 27, 2026

All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.

The Black Friday deals have arrived! Set yourself up with a turkey sandwich and a warm drink, because it's time to shop the best sale event of the year. And after the year we've had, we could all use a few bargains to cheer us up, score that upgrade we've been needing, and get a few gifts in the bag.

The Reviews team at WIRED tracks prices on our favorite gadgets year-round, and we highlight deals only on devices we’ve tested and would recommend to our own friends and family. These are the discounts that caught our eye—vetted for price hikes and fake deals. And if you’re looking for something more distinctive and gift-worthy, we’ve curated some special finds on sale.

Updated Friday, November 27, at 1:45 pm ET: We’ve added new gaming deals and our favorite deals under $100. We also updated prices and removed deals no longer available.

Additional contributors: Louryn Strampe, Scott Gilbertson, Nena Farrell, Kat Merck, Molly Higgins, Boutayna Chokrane, Luke Larsen, Harry Rabinowitz, Les Shu

Curated by Cooper Fleishman, executive commerce director. Updated Friday, November 27, at 2:30 pm ET.

The Dell XPS 13 was already a great deal, with its aggressive starting price and beautiful display. And then comes along this discount, which brings the price down to just $550. A laptop this premium for under $600 feels outrageous, even if it only comes with 8 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage. If you’re using this for work or school, you might want to consider the upgraded 16-GB model, which is also on sale for Black Friday. There’s no laptop deal quite like it right now. —Luke Larsen

Gaming laptops have gotten really expensive over the past year—to the point where I could no longer recommend any of the available options around $1,000. This deal gets close though, bringing it down to its cheapest price ever. It’s almost unheard of to find a gaming laptop with an RTX 5060 at this price, especially since this also comes with a terabyte of storage. This is a chunky boy at almost an inch thick, but hey, that’s not uncommon for gaming laptops in this price range. —Luke Larsen

I don’t normally recommend two-year-old laptops. But this is the cheapest price the Surface Laptop has dropped to this entire year, making it worth buying again. Personally, I love the 3:2 aspect ratio, which gives it a taller form factor than standard laptops. And beyond that, it’s one of the most premium-feeling laptops you can buy on the Windows side. I should note that this one isn’t the latest version with the newer chips, but for $900, it’s still great. Just know that you’re only getting 256 GB of storage. —Luke Larsen

At a full $250 off, though, it’s a must-buy. —Luke Larsen

The Mac Mini works quite well as an affordable, always-on AI box for your home, especially if you upgrade it to at least 32 GB of RAM. In terms of price, this has been the standard discount that Amazon has been offering for the past month or so, but that doesn’t mean it’s not still a strong value. —Luke Larsen

Whether you’re a video editor or wanting an at-home, all-powerful AI box for coding, the Mac Studio is an absolute champ. —Luke Larsen

Topping my guide of the best mesh Wi-Fi systems, the Wi-Fi 7 Netgear Orbi 770 Series is perfect for most families. It’s a tri-band mesh (2.4-, 5-, and 6-GHz) offering simple setup, stable and speedy internet connectivity, and expansive coverage. The stylish tower design is unobtrusive, the internal antennas ensure your whole home gets online, and it delivers the benefits of Wi-Fi 7, including MLO (Multi-Link Operation) to enable Wi-Fi 7 devices to connect on multiple bands at once. —Simon Hill

Amazon

Amazon (1-Pack)

Best Buy (1-Pack)

For folks with an Eero mesh looking to boost that backyard Wi-Fi, the Eero Outdoor 7 is a weatherproof dual-band Wi-Fi 7 router that extends coverage into your garden. Buy a pair, and you can set up a point-to-point connection to deliver up to hundreds of megabits per second, up to a half-mile away. Ideal if you need Wi-Fi in a distant barn, garage, or other outbuilding, or at the bottom of a big yard. This is the lowest price I’ve seen for this. —Simon Hill

This router will cover most homes and apartments up to around 2,000 square feet, with fast and reliable connectivity, and tops our best Wi-Fi routers guide. It’s only dual-band, so you miss out on the 6-GHz band, but you get all the other advantages of Wi-Fi 7. It also has a generous array of ports and comes with free security software and parental controls. Support for VPN service, separate IoT or guest networks, and AiMesh rounds out an excellent device. —Simon Hill

It comes in a number of different sizes, colors, and styles, and the laminated top protects against spills. It’s not the simplest to set up, but as our testers have verified, the FlexiSpot EN1 makes up for it by being such an affordable upgrade to your home office ergonomics. —Luke Larsen

Don’t rely solely on cloud storage. For sensitive documents, photos, and other files, keep them private by storing them on a NAS server at home. WIRED reviewer Simon Hill guides you through setting one up, starting with the NAS DH4300 Plus. He found it easy to install, and you can access it remotely if it’s connected to the internet. It has four bays, so you can put in four SSDs (up to 128 TB). It also works great for backing up your computers. —Les Shu

Beauty tech titan CurrentBody's Black Friday deals are live and run until December 8. Most of the brand's products are 20 percent off, including bundles. While we haven’t reviewed every bundle, we’ve tested the majority of CurrentBody's devices, and they’re consistently among our top recommendations. The Series 3, for example, is one of the best LED face masks on the market, and the LED Hair Growth Helmet has delivered some of the most noticeable results we've seen in testing.

CurrentBody gadgets aren’t cheap, so I almost always recommend waiting for a sale. And if there’s one time to shop, it’s Black Friday. For more bargains, check out our roundup of the Best Black Friday Deals.

CurrentBody

CurrentBody

Shop

I already loved the Series 2, but the latest Series 3 is in a different league. The soft, flexible silicone mask now features three additional wavelengths: blue (415 nm), green (532 nm), and yellow (590). That means it can tackle a wider range of skin concerns, including acne, hyperpigmentation, and scarring. It also significantly ups the LED count, from 236 to 750 bulbs, and increases irradiance to 40 mW/cm².

You get four preset treatments that cycle through different wavelengths, plus MyDose, which lets you customize your session including the wavelengths used and treatment time. I have yet to see another LED mask offer this level of customization and variety at this price. Don't get me wrong; it’s still a pricey skincare gadget, even with a discount, but I’d take advantage of this deal, since we're unlikely to see a better one anytime soon.

CurrentBody

CurrentBody

CurrentBody’s LED Hair Growth Helmet is our favorite at-home treatment for hair loss. It’s cordless, Bluetooth-enabled, and available in two sizes for a more comfortable fit. You only need to wear it for 10 minutes a day, and CurrentBody has thought of the little things that make sticking to a routine easier: cushy earmuffs, a removable faux leather lining, and even built-in music playback, so you don't have to sit alone with your thoughts while you grow out your hair.

Best of all, WIRED reviewer Molly Higgins and her balding roommate both noticed visible results after 12 weeks of consistent use. Molly reported thicker hair, less breakage, and fewer strands caught in her hairbrush; her hairstylist noticed, too. Molly's roommate spotted new baby hairs sprouting across his scalp. This discount makes the splurge a little less extravagant.

Black Friday is officially here, and plenty of great deals are live. Several walking pads are currently marked down, and with winter coming, now is the ideal time to take advantage of the discount. I, for one, have already started prepping my hibernation cave by stocking happy lights, arts and crafts, and a brand-new walking pad.

Our Favorite Unbound Merino Wool T-Shirts Are on Sale for Black Friday

Wired November 27, 2026

All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.

Merino Wool May be a super fiber well worth owning, but it isn't cheap. Right now, one of my favorite merino wool companies, Unbound Merino, is having its once-a-year sale. Unbound Merino's Black Friday sale is a great chance to round out your travel wardrobe with some excellent merino wool. Better hurry though, unlike most sales this time of year, Unbound Merino's Black Friday sale ends tonight.

From casual, everyday T-shirts, to underwear, socks, and great merino travel pants, Unbound has a little something for everyone. We've combed through the site and found a few of our favorite deals. Be sure to see our guide to the Best Merino Wool T-shirts, Best Merino Wool Clothes, and the Best Base Layers for more great merino wool options.

What’s So Great About Merino Wool?

Merino wool is great because you're stealing a sheep's ability to keep itself warm or cool based on the temperatures it's in. This is a process often referred to as thermoregulation. Merino sheep have thinner, softer wool than what most people think of when they think of wool. The sheep evolved this soft coat to keep them comfortable across a wide range of temperatures. The result is a fabric that's comfortable to wear next to your skin. For the softest tees, look for fabrics that are either superfine or ultrafine—anything 17 µm or higher—like Unbound's T-shirts.

Wool is sustainable, too. One sheep can produce 4 to 5 pounds of wool per year. While cotton has its place, and so does the occasional synthetic garment, merino wool is a remarkable fabric that's the cornerstone of my wardrobe. I don't think you can have too many merino pieces in your closet, but they’re not cheap, which is why we're featuring these deals.

What’s So Great About Unbound Merino?

I like Unbound's T-shirts because they're 100 percent merino wool, no synthetics involved. That means all the antibacterial, odor-resistant, moisture-wicking, temperature-regulating goodness of merino wool … just works. I've found Unbound's T-shirts in particular to be very quick-drying and wrinkle resistant, two of the reasons I think they're the best merino T-shirts for travel. The company's pants also have a very high wool percentage (95 percent), and they roll up nicely, making them very packable. Do you need special travel clothing? No, but Unbound's merino wool is naturally odor-resistant, which means you need fewer pieces in your bag. The company also offers a 30-day guarantee. If you don't like it, you can send it back.

How to Care for Merino Wool

Most merino products come with care instructions. Unbound Merino's T-shirts should be washed cold with like colors, then laid flat to dry. Whatever you do, don't bleach them and don't tumble dry them. The latter is especially destructive. I do it to every wool T-shirt I test, and it makes me sad, but I know some of you won't listen and will do it anyway, so I have to know what happens so I can warn you. Don't tumble dry. Just put it on a drying rack. It doesn't take more than a day. Seriously, you just spent $80 (on sale!) on a T-shirt; take care of it. Properly cared for, high-quality merino clothing like Unbound's is incredibly durable and will last for years. Throw it in the dryer and the pilling starts almost immediately.

Do I always lay them flat to dry? No. When traveling I usually hand-wash in the sink and then drape them over the shower curtain rod to dry, which hasn't seemed to have much negative impact. The issues with hanging wool to dry is that it will stretch out from the water weight. This is particularly true with 100 percent merino, like Unbound's T-shirts.

I've never had a problem storing merino in my closet between wears, but for long-term storage, I recommend you take precautions against moths, which are notorious for eating holes in wool. I have lost merino garments to moths. I make sure to wash and thoroughly dry whatever I am storing, then I seal it in a compression bag. Another option is to put your merino garment in a cotton bag or otherwise wrap it in cotton and then put it in a plastic bin. It's very important to make sure that the garment is completely dry before using any of these storage methods; otherwise your wool will smell musty and moldy. Other options include storing your garment in a cedar chest, which is a good natural deterrent for moths, or use moth traps or lavender sachets, which will repel the moths.

Unbound Merino

Shop (Unbound Merino Men’s)

Unbound Merino (Unbound Merino Women’s)

Unbound's T-shirts were my introduction to the brand, and they're still one of my favorite merino T-shirts. This T-shirt is incredibly soft, and because it's 100 percent merino wool, it'll stay odor-free for ages—as long as five or six days in my testing (depending on local temps, what you're doing, etc). Unbound's crew neck merino T-shirt has a relaxed, casual cut. It's not going for the technical look you'll get from many outdoor brands. It's also lightweight and packs down to a tiny ball, which is perfect if you're looking to simplify down to one bag. (Really, is there any other way to travel?)

The final thing I love about these is how fast they dry. In most climates, you can give it a wash in the sink at night, roll it up in a towel, wring it dry, lay it out flat, and it'll be dry by morning. If they have a downside, it's that Unbound's T-shirts do need to be babied a little. To help them last a long time I recommend hand washing and line-drying. Also note that while I like the merino crew neck, the V-neck is also on sale for $88 ($10 off).

These have a more formal look, what you might call slacks if you are a certain type of person. You might even be able to pull off going to office in them, but I'd sooner chew my leg off than work in an office, so I don't really know. I can say I've worn them to nice restaurants without a second look, and yet they don't scream “I've got money” when you're stumbling back to your hotel room in Prague at 4 am.

As you would expect from anything Unbound makes, these pack down fantastically small. You can pack two pairs of these for every pair of jeans. Again, for serious travelers looking to live out of a single carry-on bag, that's huge. The only downside is that these are on the thin side, not something you'd want to wear alone in cold climates. If you're like me and have to deal with winter, throw a good base layer underneath them and you'll be fine. The slim fit pant is also on sale if that's more your style.

If you want something a little different, this is the other Switch 2 bundle that’s on sale. Once again, you get a Nintendo Switch 2 system and three months of Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership, but this time it’s paired with the Nintendo Switch Sports Resort game.

This title includes all your old Wii Sports favorites (Tennis, Golf, Bowling, and Boxing), everything from Wii Sports Resort (Archery, Basketball, Table Tennis, Power Cruising, and Prop Plane), and three new options (Volleyball, Skateboarding, and Thumb Wrestling). This bundle is available for $530, which is around $28 off the usual price.

There are several deals on Switch 2 games at $20 off the usual price, so Black Friday is a good time to fill out your library before the holidays. These discounts also apply to the original Switch versions of Metroid Prime 4: Beyond and Super Mario Party Jamboree .

There are also even bigger discounts on several third-party Nintendo Switch 2 games, such as:

Belkin

I’m often asked if Dyson products are really worth the money. As WIRED’s resident vacuum tester, I’ve tried every recent Dyson vacuum—from the newest, most powerful model to the long-favored V15 Detect—and I have a lot of thoughts on which ones you should buy and at what price. The best time to shop is during sale season, and lucky for you, Dyson Black Friday deals have arrived for you to scoop up a new stick vacuum or even a handy robot vacuum.

If a new vacuum is on your wishlist this holiday season, or a loved one's (my dad is obsessed with the Dyson), then Black Friday is your best shot at a great deal ahead of the holiday season. Here's the best sales happening on Dyson vacuums I've tested and love.

Want more deals? Check out our guide to the Best Black Friday Deals; our team is actively hunting all weekend long. Want more robot vacuum options? Check out the Best Roborock Black Friday Deals.

Updated November 27, 2027: This story has been updated for Black Friday with more deals, and we checked that prices are still accurate.

Dyson

Amazon

Dyson (with Floor Dok)

Amazon (Submarine)

Dyson (Submarine)

If you’re going to buy a Dyson vacuum on sale, you might as well go for one of the better ones. The V16 Piston Animal is Dyson’s most powerful stick vacuum, with 315 air-watts of power, some nice quality-of-life improvements in the body design, and an option to add the Submarine 2.0 mop head. I really liked this vacuum for the design upgrades and power level, but the price tag can be hard to stomach. It’s on sale fairly regularly, and there are a few different on-sale combos: The base vacuum is $180 off, bundling it with the Submarine head is $200 off, and the option with the charging Floor Dok is also $200 off. I love the Submarine head, but while I haven’t tested the vacuum with the Floor Dok yet, it’s the accessory I want most—having your cordless vacuum fully charged whenever you want it, and somewhere to store it, is really handy.

Dyson

Dyson (With Car Cleaning Kit)

If you want a cheaper vacuum that still comes with two cleaner heads, the older Dyson V15 Detect is also already on sale ($599), and it's even bundled with the Car Cleaning Kit, meaning three extra attachments. The V15 was our top Dyson vacuum pick for a long time because it's more affordable than the Gen5Detect and V16, but still packs two cleaner heads (the Digital Motorbar for carpet and Fluffy Optic for hard floors) and has 240 air-watts of suction (almost 100 more than the V10 Konical and other cheaper Dyson vacuums). It's a great all-around vacuum, and this bundle option gets you great extra attachments.

Dyson

Amazon

Best Buy

Dyson had two different budget vacuums come out this year, but the V10 Konical was my favorite of the two. It has a modified version of the All Floor Cones cleaner head you'll find on the much more expensive V16 Piston Animal and did a great job in my tests; overall, it actually scored a little higher than the V15 Detect when tested side by side. It's often on sale for $400, but you can find it for an even better $350 right now during Black Friday.

Dyson

Amazon

Dyson

The PencilVac is incredibly handy and compact, and great if you're trying to do quick pickups daily on hard floors. You won't want it if you have any kind of rug or carpet, since it's only designed for hard flooring, but I did find it incredibly easy to grab and use for constant litter trails in my house. It's incredibly lightweight and a great fit for anyone with mobility or strength concerns. If these features speak to you, this is a great time to buy, as it's already on sale.

Dyson

Dyson

Best Buy

This wet floor cleaner is often on sale for around $400, so it's not a huge surprise to see this deal ahead of Black Friday. The Dyson Clean+Wash is primarily a wet floor cleaner, but it can do dry cleans, too, and does not use a filter you inevitably need to keep clean. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck noticed no weird smells in three months of use. It's similar to the Dyson WashG1, with a self-propelled design that makes it easy to push around the room, and it does a good job scrubbing floors clean. Keep in mind that it's not great for dry debris, since it’s just rolling, not sucking.

Dyson

Amazon

Best Buy

Dyson

The Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai came out earlier this year and is one of my favorite robot vacuums from the brand. That's including the newer Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV I’m currently testing, which hasn't blown me away as a better investment. (It actually failed my corner test completely, which vacuums in that price range should not do.)

It is a great time to buy a new pair of headphones. Brands have largely finished launching their latest models for the year, and I'm seeing some stellar Black Friday headphone deals on new and older headphones alike. I've been reviewing headphones (and covering Black Friday deals) for more than four years, so I have a good handle on what's worth opening your wallet for. (Spoilers: it's Sony and Bose this year).

All the deals below are WIRED-tested products we stand by, including wireless earbuds and over-ear headphones. For more Black Friday deals, check out our guides to the Best Black Friday TV Deals and the Best Black Friday Mattress Deals.

Amazon

Walmart

Apple

Apple AirPods Pro 3 are the best wireless earbuds not only for anyone with an iPhone—but also for anyone who wants to keep things simple. They sound great and have some of the best active-noise-canceling (ANC) and transparency modes on the market. They also seamlessly sync with all of your Apple devices. At $100 off, it's the lowest price they've ever been at.

Soundcore by Anker

Amazon

Shop (Soundcore)

This is the lowest price I’ve ever seen on one of my favorite pairs of wireless earbuds. The Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro have one magic trick: call quality. To put it simply, I sound better talking on calls using these earbuds than any other I’ve tested, and it’s not a close competition. Beyond that, they’re solid all-rounders, with good noise-canceling, sound quality, and versatility.

Amazon

Best Buy

Want workout earbuds that won't fall out? Get these Beats Powerbeats Pro 2. They're some of the more secure-fitting earbuds I've ever tested. Amazon

While the automated noise-canceling isn't the best, it's hard to fault them at this new low price.

Best Buy

Best Buy

Best Buy

These are the best wireless headphones we've ever tested, featuring some of the best noise canceling you can buy, paired with 30 hours of battery power. They're the latest in the lineup, with a new, smaller case and memory-foam—augmented folding ear cups that make them easy to pack for travel.

Best Buy

These earbuds weigh just 5.5 grams per bud—25 percent smaller and 20 percent lighter than the previous model. Our reviewer loved them for their detailed and balanced sound, though he did find the noise canceling and call quality to be underwhelming. If you prioritize musical detail over bass, however, this sale makes them an excellent option to grab for your holiday travels.

Breville

Best Buy

This Breville is the best semiautomatic espresso machine for most people, and reviewer Julian Chokkattu has been using the longtime WIRED favorite for seven years. We love its consistent pressure, steam wand, and built-in grinder, as well as the all-metal construction that's easy to clean. Buy it now and impress your in-laws at Thanksgiving with espresso martinis and latte art.

Best Buy

Samsung

Best Buy

Its high price was one of our reviewer’s main complaints, so if you've been in the market, consider this your lucky day.

Welcome to the Repair Café, Where Neighbors Fight Throwaway Culture

Wired November 27, 2026

This story originally appeared on Grist and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.

On an unusually cool and rainy Saturday morning in Decatur, Georgia, dozens of people filed into a warehouse at the back of a church parking lot, their arms full of what a less hopeful group might call junk. Some carried broken lamps, glitching electronics, or cracked furniture. Others walked in with toolboxes, multimeters for testing electric currents, and cans of WD-40. Beneath extension cords dangling from the rafters, they sorted themselves into smaller groups: the volunteer electricians, tailors, luthiers, carpenters, and at least one cutler (knife sharpener), commandeering nearby worktables and passersby as needed.

That’s how Lilly Pettus ended up shoulder to shoulder with three strangers, their hands all pressing together the pieces of her family’s cracked dining room chair as wood glue hardened and a volunteer tightened a clamp.

“This is so interesting,” a giddy Pettus said, inspecting for the first time the joints, one of them broken, that held together the chair she’d owned for decades. “You never even know how furniture is put together.”

This is Decatur’s semi-regular repair café, one of a few hundred meetings like it across the United States. More Americans than ever are turning to these community gatherings to fix what they already own, resisting the influence of companies that sell everything from hiking boots to smartphones and hot water boilers and that push for replacement over repair. One consequence of this throwaway economy is an increase in greenhouse gas emissions from manufacturing that threatens to intensify climate change.

Yet, organizers and volunteers consider repair cafés to be more than a relatively small climate solution. As inflation rises and wages stagnate, the meetups connect people to a movement with the ambitious goal of changing the fundamentals of America’s consumer economy.

At the Decatur repair café, volunteers, wearing green shirts with “I can probably fix that” printed on the back, offered their skills free of charge as patrons observed. A young father of a toddler and squirmy baby watched as a volunteer replaced a switch on a favorite mid-century modern lamp worn out by the older child’s repeated clicking. Murmurs of excitement rippled around the building as the acrid smell of a spot welding project wafted through.

Pettus’ broken chair held in its wood her family’s story. Soon after she and her husband were married in 1996, they began a search for a dining room set. Pettus wanted the chairs to be comfortable for her entire family, but one of her brothers is nearly 7 feet tall, and another just a few inches shorter. “We are not a tiny family,” Pettus said. “We are a big family.”

Pettus also thought of one of her children who’d interned at the Environmental Protection Agency and shared his concerns with Pettus about pollution and climate change. Then, after months of the broken chair cluttering the family’s house, Pettus was running Saturday morning errands when she passed the Decatur repair café. She drove the half-mile home to grab the chair and decided to give it a second chance.

“When a product breaks and you have to throw it away, it’s very lonely,” said Martine Postma, director of Repair Café International, a Netherlands-based network of 4,000 cafés. “ It’s easier to just go on the internet and order a new item which will come to your doorstep in 24 hours, but that’s also a very lonely, disconnected activity.”

Postma, a former journalist with the demeanor of an unflappable librarian, founded her organization in 2010 after the birth of her second child magnified her fears about the planet’s future. “Markets are flooded with trash—with cheap products that we don’t need and that do not work,” Postma said. “They break, and they contribute nothing to our well-being. They just contribute waste.”

Repair cafés appear to be inspiring people to use their stuff longer. In 2025, they prevented nearly 2 million pounds of waste—the equivalent of more than 100 fully loaded Boeing 747 aircraft—according to Repair Café International, and reduced greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to the average consumption of about 1,000 Dutch families.

Postma, Pettus, and millions of others often smack into obstacles when they try to fix their own stuff. Broken products are increasingly difficult to repair, according to a report from the Federal Trade Commission titled “Nixing the Fix.” The report details how Americans are incentivized to “replace products before the end of their useful lives” by companies that decide to make repairs less safe, limit the availability of parts, lock software and firmware, or even “disparage” independent repair.

In 2023, California, Colorado, Minnesota, and New York passed “right to repair” legislation meant to encourage repair over replacement. A year later the European Union passed a similar directive. Postma and other organizers consider the cafés a natural place for activism to push for right-to-repair measures, although Postma hopes for more sweeping changes in Europe, like a tax on raw materials. She argued it would limit emissions and bolster repair shops, even if it increases the cost of products.

“ I feel for the objects around me. I feel sorry for them if they’re broken,” she said. “I want to make repairing a normal thing in everyday life once more.”

According to Postma, repairing goods is more common in relatively poor countries where replacing them can be especially difficult and expensive. It’s in wealthy countries that repair cafés are thriving, but they’re not at all uniform. Each reflects the surrounding area and its socioeconomics.

On a Sunday afternoon in the Collier Heights neighborhood of Atlanta, volunteers brought most of their own tools to the basement of a building owned by a Seventh-Day Adventist Church, setting them on white plastic folding tables atop a light pink carpet. The café looked much different from the one a 30-minute drive across the city in Decatur. The median annual household income in the mostly Black Collier Heights neighborhood is roughly $40,000 lower than in Decatur. Many people who brought items wanted them fixed less for sentimental reason, and more so they could keep using them.

Gale Pines walked in with a red air fryer that had stopped working after they used it to dehydrate ginger. When their oven ran, Pines said, it heated the entire kitchen. So, while in nursing school, they cooked many of their evening meals in the air fryer, most often chicken nuggets and fries.

Pines recently graduated but had trouble finding a job and couldn’t afford to buy a new $100 air fryer. “It’s just hard to exist,” Pines said. “I don’t really have a very big support network outside of my friends.”

One of Pines’ housemates told them about Collier Heights’ repair café. They keep a bag of broken electronics in the garage that they’d prefer not to send to a landfill. “Being in the height of climate collapse we can’t just keep buying new stuff all the time, both for the economy and for our material scarcity,” Pines said.

When a volunteer at the Collier Heights repair café opened up the air fryer, they quickly discovered the problem: a bad capacitor. Another volunteer had brought a replacement part, and the two of them made the fix as Pines watched, impressed, but unable to follow the relatively complex repair. Pines felt OK that they hadn’t learned how to fix the air fryer themself.

“ To just be around people that want to help other people with the skills that they have, that’s value that is really important to me and something that I try to do as well,” Pines said. “If somebody in my community has a question about their medication or something and can’t afford to go to the doctor, I’m happy to answer any questions that people have.”

Another volunteer, Lew Lefton, said he thought that the satisfaction humans draw from making and fixing things has largely been lost, but apocalyptic threats like climate change and artificial intelligence have driven many people toward rediscovering more basic, human skills that are key to survival. People who come to a repair café have a different way to view the future, according to Lefton, especially if they learn something or volunteer themselves. “If the world ends,” he said, “at least I’ll know how to fix a motor.”

Back in Decatur, Pettus left the repair café with a newly sturdy chair. A screw and some glue fixed the crack around the joint, but the chair still needed upholstery work. Someone Pettus met at the café, who had provided one of the sets of hands that held her chair together as the glue set, advised her on where to buy fabric. Pettus thought she might bring the chair back to the repair café for help reupholstering its seat cushion.

“The beauty of it,” Pettus said, “was that I actually was able to learn more about the chair. It was a great experience to know that—I’m not gonna say I birthed it, I of course did not—but I actually had something to do with helping to get it put back together.”

I love a good e-reader, and Black Friday is one of the best times to buy a new one. I've scoured the internet and my own guides to find the best Black Friday Kindle and e-reader deals on devices that are worth buying at full price, making these sales something you shouldn't miss if you're in the market for a new e-reader (or want to gift one to someone!)

Great e-readers have e-paper screens that are easier on your eyes than reading on a smartphone or tablet screen, but allow you to bring hundreds of books with you without worrying about damaging any book spines (or your own spine from carrying so many books around). You can connect these to the Libby app to get library ebooks, too, letting your reading run wild and literally free.

Here's the best e-reader deals happening right now as the Black Friday kicks off. Curious about the best models to buy, regardless of what's on sale? Catch my guides to the Best Kindles and Best E-Readers That Aren't a Kindle. Looking for more sales? Don't miss our guide on the Absolute Best Black Friday Deals.

Amazon

Amazon

Amazon (Signature)

The best all-around Kindle is consistently the Kindle Paperwhite. Right now, only the older 12thgeneration that came out in 2024 is on sale. The Paperwhite used to cost $160, but a $30 discount off the original price makes this a deal worth shopping.

But that doesn’t mean you have to abandon your dreams of getting a great deal on a great iPad this year. The best Black Friday iPad deals could be exactly what you've been waiting for.

The iPad Air is the in-between iPad. It’s not as cheap as the base iPad, nor does it have the Tandem OLED screen and high-end features of the iPad Pro. And yet, I think it’s the iPad people should buy if they plan to use it for work. That’s mainly because it has a powerful M4 chip and can connect to a Magic Keyboard with full trackpad support. And while the $649 sale isn’t particularly rare, it’s not a bad price for a tablet that works well as a laptop replacement.

iPad Pro 11-inch for $1,049: It’s surprising that the iPad Pro hasn’t been heavily discounted at all for Black Friday. At $1,049, it’s cheaper than the 13-inch MacBook Air, which uses the same M5 chip. The difference? You still have to buy the Magic Keyboard separately to pair with the iPad Pro. All in all, the iPad ends up being much more expensive.

iPad Mini (2024) for $499: Like the newer iPad Mini, the 2024 model is also $100 off. The upgrades in the 2026 model are worth the money, but if you just need something simple to take notes or read books on, this previous model will do the trick.

iPad Pro 13-Inch for $1,697: The 13-inch iPad Pro has been fluctuating in price since we started monitoring Black Friday sales. At one point, it was as low as $1,349—a terrific deal for Apple’s flagship iPad. It is a bit of a niche tablet because of the price alone, but if you want an iPad that can properly replace a high-end laptop, the 13-inch model is big enough (and fast enough) for the job. The sale has ended since we last checked, but we’re keeping it on our list—it’s worth checking in case it goes on sale again.

I’ve been cooking dinner for myself (and/or my family) nearly every night for the past 27 years. Suffice it to say I've learned some kitchen tips and tricks during those decades—especially about what is and isn't worth taking up valuable counter space.

Some of my favorite kitchen gadgets may not be the most flashy (a measuring cup, a mesh cloth, a cast-iron pan). Instead, they're the kinds of things that really matter when you cook a lot, whether in service of keeping things clean and organized, or sharp, or preserving your hard work by freezing leftovers for a future busy night.

I've also thrown in a couple of fun nice-to-haves, including a kit for making Giada De Laurentiis' viral (and highly recommended!) sheet-pan lasagna and a 500-piece puzzle that may send you on a soup-making side quest.

For more gift ideas, check out our Best Gifts Under $100, Best Tech Gifts, and Best Gifts Under $25.

Cast iron cookware is unparalleled for its heat retention, durability, and nonstick nature, so long as you keep it well seasoned. But it's also heavy and often difficult to maneuver. You could always use lightweight carbon steel, made with an iron-carbon alloy, but it doesn't really act like cast iron in that it's highly variable in terms of heat. Field's heirloom-quality pans are modeled on smooth vintage designs and are just as lightweight as stainless steel, yet retain all the benefits of cast iron. WIRED operations manager Scott Gilberston likes them a lot, and so do I.
